analysis.title: European Equity Daily, 27 October
key_insights: Jefferies refreshed its EMEA Franchise Picks (highest-conviction list across 800+ covered stocks), adding Bridgepoint, DWS, Endeavour Mining, Genmab, GTT, Inditex, Kingspan, Nestlé and Sandoz.
Midcap Top Picks list updated with 30 high-conviction ideas from a universe of 500+ pan-European mid caps.

Iberian banks have de-rated on rising market volatility, but Jefferies stays positive on strong loan growth, resilient asset quality and higher-for-longer rates. Bankinter upgraded to Buy, Santander downgraded to Hold.

Imperial Brands downgraded to Hold: a multi-year series of German excise hikes, rising illicit trade and accelerating volume declines drive estimate cuts and raise the risk of a FY27 expectations reset.
Payments and FinTech: sentiment is cautious, with agentic commerce raising terminal-value concerns. Jefferies favours Adyen, Wise, Nayax and Boku where valuation already reflects this risk.
Kingspan: investors underestimate Advnsys's role in the equity story. Jefferies argues the converged data-centre solution gives exposure to a fast-growing end-market.
IG Group stays Buy: valuation over-discounts the earnings impact of an adverse regulatory outcome for Underdog and the execution risk on revenue retention optimisation.
Middle East Lodging: investor meetings and site visits point to a cautious near-term outlook, with geopolitical and macro uncertainty clouding the timing of RevPAR recovery and NUG growth.

US Specialty Pharma: animal health may be entering a new regime as competition erodes pricing power. Zoetis and Elanco downgraded, while diagnostics are seen as structurally advantaged with IDEXX supported by double-digit EPS growth.
Japan quant: reform agenda shifts from balance sheet optimisation to profitability and capital allocation. Incremental ROIC is the preferred guide to future winners.

China data centre stocks sold off alongside US neoclouds, but business models differ: long-term hyperscaler contracts, customer-funded GPUs and low-cost financing reduce risk. VNET remains the preferred pick.

AstraZeneca ESMO event was broadly reassuring with strong data in SCLC, bladder and gastric cancer. AVANZAR is delayed into 1Q27 due to slower PFS event accrual, with censoring normal and management still optimistic.
Schneider Electric delivered a strong Q3 and another FY guidance upgrade, with the equity overhang removed. Estimates raised low single digit and PT raised to €329.
UK Defence: The Sunday Times reported the Chancellor will announce billions more for defence in Wednesday's Budget. BAB and QQ are most exposed to UK MoD spending, CHRT also meaningfully leveraged.

Novartis 3Q sales slightly ahead (Cosentyx beat, Pluvicto miss); core operating income and core EPS 8% ahead of consensus. 2026 profit guidance raised, implying about 300bps consensus profit upgrades at the midpoint.
INFICON posted a record quarter: sales $233m (+42% YoY), 14% above consensus, operating margin 25.5%, 40% EBIT beat and guidance raised about 20% at the midpoint.
SIG Group beat Q3 EBIT by 12% and raised 2026 EBIT margin guidance to 16-16.5% and medium-term margin to above 18%.

Spain softened proposed data-centre power rules (renewable requirement starts at 60% instead of 80%), positive for Merlin Properties. The draft decree is targeted for approval before the 29 November election.
Galp is down about 10% after terminating Moeve downstream combination talks, despite a Q3 EBITDA beat and FY26 guidance upgrade.
US OCTG prices rose 9% (seamless) and 10% (welded) in October, the biggest monthly dollar gain since July 2008, positive for Tenaris and Vallourec.
Cancom cut FY26 revenue guidance by 5.5% at the midpoint on weak orders and project delays, leaving profit targets unchanged. Q3 revenue was 2% below consensus.
Computacenter pulled forward another positive trading statement seven weeks after an 18% estimate upgrade.
European AI enablers (semicap, grids, power) are a focus: European data-centre capacity could rise about 75% by 2030 per ECIPE discussion.
Brazil: Lula's re-election means fiscal adjustment of about 4pp of GDP looks politically difficult, with a recession probability above 50% for 2027 per an expert call.
Macau October GGR is tracking down 9-11% YoY, worse than Jefferies' earlier 6-10% estimate.
CATL downgraded (A-share to Hold, H-share to Underperform) on weaker EV/ESS demand and pricing pressure from 2027. Eve Energy PT cut 28% to Rmb46.
US 10-year Treasury yield fell 8bps to 5.00% last week while the S&P 500 fell 0.5% (REIT weekly note).
Bank of Canada decides Wednesday with the market largely anticipating a hike, which Jefferies' John Aiken views as a misstep.
US midterms are a major conference theme, with Jefferies hosting calls on 27 October, 30 October and 4 November.
